H-infinity output-feedback synthesis (experimental)

Source: R/robust.R
ctrl_hinfsyn.Rd

Compute a stabilizing controller with closed-loop \(\|T_{zw}\|_\infty < \gamma\) for a continuous time generalized plant (see ctrl_lft()), and optionally search for the smallest achievable \(\gamma\) by bisection.

Usage

ctrl_hinfsyn(P, nmeas, ncon, gamma = NULL, tol = 0.001, gamma_range = NULL)

Arguments

P

Generalized plant.

nmeas, ncon

Numbers of measurements and controls.

gamma

Target level; NULL searches for the optimum.

tol

Relative bisection tolerance.

gamma_range

Optional c(lower, upper) search interval.

Value

An object of class c("ctrl_synthesis", "ctrl_controller") with K, closed_loop, gamma (the level used), norm (certified closed-loop H-infinity norm), X, Y, history (bisection log) and method.

Details

Scope. Continuous time only, with \(D_{11} = 0\), \(D_{12}\) full column rank, \(D_{21}\) full row rank, \((A, B_2)\) stabilizable and \((C_2, A)\) detectable; arbitrary \(D_{22}\) is handled with a loop shift. Plants with \(D_{11} \ne 0\) (for example mixed-sensitivity designs with a biproper sensitivity weight) are rejected, as are discrete time plants.

Algorithm. The plant is first normalized with orthogonal transformations of z and w and invertible scalings of u and y so that \(D_{12} = [0; I]\) and \(D_{21} = [0, I]\) (these leave the H-infinity norm unchanged). For a given \(\gamma\), the two H-infinity Riccati equations of Glover and Doyle (1988) are solved with ctrl_care() on indefinite weights; \(\gamma\) is feasible when both stabilizing solutions exist, \(X_\infty \succeq 0\), \(Y_\infty \succeq 0\) and \(\rho(X_\infty Y_\infty) < \gamma^2\). The central controller is then \(A_K = A + \gamma^{-2} B_1 B_1^\top X_\infty + B_2 F_\infty + Z_\infty L_\infty (C_2 + \gamma^{-2} D_{21} B_1^\top X_\infty)\), \(B_K = -Z_\infty L_\infty\), \(C_K = F_\infty\), \(D_K = 0\), with \(F_\infty = -(D_{12}^\top C_1 + B_2^\top X_\infty)\), \(L_\infty = -(B_1 D_{21}^\top + Y_\infty C_2^\top)\) and \(Z_\infty = (I - \gamma^{-2} Y_\infty X_\infty)^{-1}\).

Certification. Every returned controller is checked independently: the closed loop must be internally stable and its H-infinity norm, computed with ctrl_norm() (Bruinsma-Steinbuch, a different algorithm), must be below \(\gamma\). If the check fails, an error is raised instead of returning an uncertified controller. The bisection stops at relative tolerance tol and returns the controller for the smallest feasible \(\gamma\) found, which is slightly suboptimal by design: the central controller becomes ill-conditioned at the optimum. When the H2 optimal controller already gives a zero closed-loop norm, the optimum zero is attained and that controller is returned with gamma = 0.

References

Glover, K. and Doyle, J. C. (1988). State-space formulae for all stabilizing controllers that satisfy an H-infinity norm bound and relations to risk sensitivity. Systems and Control Letters, 11, 167-172.

Examples

A <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE)
P <- ctrl_ss(A, cbind(diag(2), 0, c(0, 1)),
             rbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 0), c(1, 0)),
             rbind(c(0, 0, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 0, 1), c(0, 0, 1, 0)))
hinf <- ctrl_hinfsyn(P, nmeas = 1, ncon = 1)
c(gamma = hinf$gamma, certified_norm = hinf$norm)
#>          gamma certified_norm 
#>       2.896528       2.896523
